Elias tucked the note into his coat, already planning the trip to the coastal village where the sailor’s love had waited all those years.", "w02": "凌晨四点的城市还浸在半梦半醒的灰蓝色里，路灯把柏油路照得发暖，偶尔有晚归的代驾骑着小车滑过，车铃轻响一声就被风卷走。沿街的早餐铺已经亮了灯，蒸笼掀开时腾起的白汽裹着麦香飘出半条街，环卫工的扫帚扫过路面，发出沙沙的轻响。远处的高楼还隐在夜色里，只有零星几扇窗亮着灯，整座城市安静得像在轻轻呼吸，等着第一缕晨光把它唤醒。", "w03": "- Recursion is when you solve a big problem by breaking it into tiny, identical little problems that are just smaller versions of the original big one.\n- For example, if you want to count how many candies are in a big jar, you can take out one candy, then count how many are left in the jar — that smaller count problem uses the exact same trick you used for the big jar.\n- Every recursion needs a clear 'base case' where you stop breaking the problem into smaller pieces, like when there are zero candies left in the jar, you know the count is zero, no more tricks needed."}
